c0010.en: ▸ Green cells are editable: assigned to, time, notes.

c0017.en: Designed by John Guerrero — chef and restaurant consultant since 2010, in professional kitchens since age 17 · johnguerrero.es

c0028.en: Clean uniform and work shoes, fresh apron, hair tied back and covered (cap or hairnet)

c0030.en: No hand/arm jewelry except a plain band; nails short, clean, no polish or acrylics

c0031.en: Cover cuts and wounds with a waterproof, brightly colored bandage and a glove on top

c0032.en: Wash hands at the handwashing sink on arrival and at every change of task: soap, hot water (at least 100 °F, FDA Food Code 5-202.12) and single-use paper towels

c0033.en: Check no one has vomiting, diarrhea, jaundice, sore throat with fever or an infected cut; if so, no food handling (FDA 2-201.11)

c0035.en: Turn on the exhaust hood and ventilate the kitchen BEFORE lighting anything else

c0087.en: Use the dropdown: ✓, — or N/A. N/A = not applicable, comes out of the total; — = not done, counts as pending.

c0114.en: Raw red meat and poultry, whole cuts

c0116.en: Portion BEFORE freezing: never thaw and refreeze

c0119.en: More exposed surface: it goes rancid and oxidizes much sooner than a whole cut

c0125.en: Fat goes rancid even when frozen: it spoils first

c0127.en: Label with the production date AND the freezing date: shelf life counts from the freezing date

c0130.en: Yeast loses strength: the dough rises poorly afterwards even if it is still safe

c0133.en: It loses texture before it loses safety; refresh it in the oven, never in the microwave

c0136.en: Blanch before freezing: unblanched, it loses color and texture within a few weeks

c0364.en: ▸ Combine them with the general checklists (01-05) for full coverage.

c0812.en: Write the report number of each inspection and the date of the next one in "Notes"

c0949.en: ▸ Each task comes with Assigned to and Due by preloaded with the kit's criteria: adjust them to your real schedule, they are green cells.

c0951.en: ▸ Everything filled in daily is GREEN: Assigned to, Due by, ✓ Done, Initials and Notes.

c0953.en: ▸ Mark ✓ in the "✓ Done" column (dropdown): that is the column that counts completed tasks.

c0955.en: ▸ The denominator counts the tasks written in the "Task" column, not a fixed number: if you add or delete tasks, the total adjusts by itself.

c0957.en: ▸ At the end of each table there are 5 free green rows INSIDE the range the counter covers: write your own tasks there.

c0958.en: ▸ If you need more, insert rows INSIDE the table (right-click → Insert), never below the last one: anything typed outside the range is not counted.

c0960.en: ▸ Sheets with formulas are protected WITHOUT a password: the input cells (the green ones) are unlocked, so calculations never get overwritten by accident.

c0961.en: ▸ You can insert and delete rows with protection on. To change the structure: Review → Unprotect Sheet.

c0980.en: Turn on HVAC / heat depending on the season

c0984.en: Turn on the POS / card terminal

c0987.en: Play background music at a suitable volume

c0989.en: Check restrooms: paper, soap, cleanliness, air freshener

c0990.en: Check cleanliness of common areas (entrance, hallways)

c0994.en: Check that menus are in order

c0995.en: Turn on displays / info screens if any

c1024.en: ▸ The daily cash count: starting bank, drawer count by denomination, POS Z report and over/short — plus the monthly log to see at a glance which days didn't balance.

c1025.en: How to use — Cash Drawer Opening

c1026.en: ▸ Count the starting bank and type the amount in the GREEN cell "Starting bank (opening float)". The closing sheet reads it from there: no need to retype it.

c1027.en: How to use — Cash Drawer Closing

c1028.en: ▸ In "Cash Count by Denomination" fill in ONLY the "Quantity" column (number of bills or coins, whole number): the subtotal and TOTAL CASH calculate themselves. The table has US bills and coins (the penny is no longer minted but is still legal tender; a "25¢ roll" counts $10 and a "10¢ roll" $5). In the UK, Canada or Australia, unprotect the sheet (no password) and change the label and value of each row.

c1029.en: ▸ In the "Closing Summary" you only type three figures: "Card sales, excl. tips", "Other tenders + card tips paid in cash" and "POS Z report: sales + tax, excl. tips" (net sales plus sales tax, without tips or gratuities; many POS "total" lines include tips). Everything else is a formula.

c1030.en: ▸ The starting bank is deducted automatically: TOTAL COLLECTED = (cash counted − starting bank) + card sales + other.

c1031.en: ▸ OVER / SHORT = TOTAL COLLECTED − POS Z report (sales + tax, excl. tips). If the cell turns AMBER, the drawer doesn't balance: check it BEFORE signing.

c1032.en: ▸ One row per day: enter starting bank, sales by payment type, POS Z report and deposit; Total Collected and Over/Short calculate themselves and the over/short turns amber.

c1033.en: ▸ The starting bank is a balance, not a sale: the TOTALS row shows the AVERAGE starting bank of the days logged, not their sum.

c1034.en: ▸ Everything filled in daily is GREEN: Assigned to, Due by, ✓ Done, Initials, Notes, the count quantities and the summary amounts.

c1041.en: Write the starting bank in the green cell below

c1042.en: Check there is enough change (coins, small bills)

c1043.en: Check that the POS is on and open the register shift

c1044.en: Print the opening X report (start-of-day report)

c1048.en: Note issues from the previous shift

c1051.en: Deducted from cash on the "Cash Drawer Closing" sheet

c1054.en: Print the closing Z report (end-of-day report)

c1055.en: Cash count by denomination (see table below)

c1059.en: Total collected = (cash counted − starting bank) + card sales + other

c1060.en: Compare with the POS Z report → calculate the over/short

c1064.en: Prepare the bank deposit / put it in the safe

c1100.en: Enter how many bills, coins or rolls: a whole number (0 or more), no decimals.

c1113.en: "Cash Counted" is the drawer count AS IS, with the starting bank inside: Total Collected already deducts it. In TOTALS, "Starting Bank" is the AVERAGE starting bank of the days logged (a balance is not summed) and "Over/Short" is the CUMULATIVE over/short in absolute value: a +50 and a −50 make 100 of over/short, not 0. "Card Sales (no tips)" excludes tips; "Other + Tips Paid" = other tenders + card tips paid in cash from the drawer. "POS Z" = net sales + sales tax, without tips.
